column1: # Gustik partition table for the 4 MB ESP32-WROOM-32 module.
# Replaces the Arduino default (default.csv)
# application slots for over-the-air updates. This project has no OTA
# mechanism and never will - it is reflashed over USB - so the second slot
# was 1.25 MB of flash permanently doing nothing while the first was 92.8%
# full. See docs/hardware/flash-memory-map.md for the full reasoning.
# Deliberate choices
column2: do not "tidy" these without reading that document:

column1: #   - app0 keeps subtype ota_0 (not factory) so the Arduino toolchain's
#     boot_app0.bin -> otadata -> ota_0 boot path is byte-for-byte the one
#     already in use. One slot means OTA is impossible; the boot sequence is
#     unchanged. A factory-subtype slot would work only via bootloader
#     fallback
column2: which is a behaviour change for no gain.

column1: #   - otadata stays for the same reason: PlatformIO flashes boot_app0.bin to
#     0xe000 on every upload and expects a partition there.
#   - The data partition MUST stay named "spiffs" even though it holds a
#     LittleFS image: LittleFS.begin() defaults to partitionLabel "spiffs"
#     (framework-arduinoespressif32 LittleFS.h). Renaming it to "littlefs"
#     makes config.txt and the offline buffer silently unreadable.
# Sizes (a trailing "# comment" on a data row is parsed as the Flags column
# and fails the build
#   nvs      20 KB    IDF/WiFi calibration store
#   otadata  8 KB     boot slot selector
#   app0     2 MB     firmware (was 1.25 MB)
#   spiffs   1.875 MB LittleFS (was 1.375 MB)
#   coredump 64 KB    unused
# 0x210000 + 0x1E0000 + 0x10000 = 0x400000 exactly - the table fills the chip.
# Name
nvs
otadata
app0
spiffs
coredump
